transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what brings me in is that I just feel like I’m constantly running on a motor lately. I'll finish one thing at school—I teach special ed—or I'll finish a task at home, and I immediately jump right into the next thing. It's like I'm never able to just shut myself off.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot most days?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I mean, I have the usual stress from teaching, but I don't spend my days feeling anxious or worrying about things. It's not really a mental stress like that, just more of a physical inability to stop.
Do you often have trouble paying attention?

No, I wouldn't say so. I don't really have an issue focusing on things. When I'm working with my students or doing tasks around the house, I can pay attention just fine. It's really just the physical part—not being able to sit still or take a break—rather than losing my focus.
Have you had any periods where you felt unusually upbeat or energized compared with your normal self?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, like I said, I always have this constant physical energy, but it's not like I go through phases where I'm suddenly way more upbeat or energized than usual. This is just my normal everyday state. It's not really a mood thing where I'm suddenly on top of the world, I just... I just always have to be doing something. So, no, no unusual periods like that.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out generalized anxiety disorder and bipolar disorder based on absence of excessive worry, mood episodes, or clear episodic elevated mood; remaining candidate most consistent with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly hyperactive/impulsive presentation.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes persistent motor restlessness and inability to sit still, but denies the core ADHD features of inattention and functional focus problems. There is no evidence of a distinct hypomanic/manic episode or prominent generalized worry/anxiety. The presentation is most consistent with an unspecified hyperkinetic/restlessness presentation rather than classic ADHD, though ADHD was considered as the main differential given the constant 'running on a motor' complaint.
